newsitem.title: USA: Kasich - Clinton plan has no large family tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Kasich - Clinton plan has no large family tax cut.

text.p: House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich said Thursday President Clinton's proposed spending plan contains no large tax break for families.
"If American families are sitting out there hoping that they're going to get a big break as proposed by this budget, I've not really seen it," he said in an interview on CNN.

The Ohio Republican criticized the Clinton tax cut proposals for being temporary and targeted. He said their message is: "We'll let you keep a little bit more of your money but what you're going to have to do is jump through a bunch of hoops." The Clinton tax cuts are focused on tax breaks for education and children.

Clinton has proposed a $500 per child tax credit for low- and middle-income families, saving taxpayers $46 billion through 2002. He has also proposed a $1,500 tax credit or a $10,000 tax deduction for college tuition and training that would cost $36 billion.
The White House's proposal to raise the capital gains tax exclusion on home sales to $250,000 per person, or $500,000 per couple, for all Americans would save taxpayers $1.4 billion through 2002.

Clinton also proposed a maximum $5,000 tax credit for companies which give welfare recipients a job, and doubling the income limits on deductible Individual Retirement Accounts to give $5.5 billion back to taxpayers.
